questions.question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

She said that she could not believe him.

options.text: She said, “I may not believe him.”
She says, “I could not believed him.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**She said, “I cannot believe him**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct ***direct form*** of the given sentence is ' She said, “I cannot believe him.”
 
• ***Direct speech*** - She said, “I cannot believe him.”
 
• ***Indirect speech*** - She said that she could not believe him.
 
• Therefore,*** option 3*** is the correct option.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's discuss direct and indirect speech:
 
• ***Direct speech*** - Direct speech is used to describe the situation in the ***present tense*** or make it feel like it is happening now.
 
 
• ***​******For example,*** He said to her "I will come to play after finishing my homework".
 
 
 
• ***​******​Indirect speech*** - Indirect speech is used to describe the situation in ***past tense*** or make it feel like it has happened before.
 
 
• ***​******​For example,*** "He said that he will come to play after he finishes his homework".

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The secretary was noting down the dictation.

options.text: The dictation was noted down by the secretary.
The notes were noted by the secretary.
The dictation was being noted down by the secretary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The dictation was being noted down by the secretary**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• ***Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object. (Active Voice)***
 
• ***Subject(Objective Case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice) ***
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• He was riding a bike.
 
• A bike was being ridden by him. 
 
 
 
• Here, in the given sentence ';was noting down' will be changed into ';was being noted down'. **​**
 
• ***​​​******Active voice*** - The secretary was noting down the dictation.
 
• ***Passive voice*** -** The dictation was being noted down by the secretary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's discuss information about ***active and passive voice***:
 
• Active voice - An ***active voice*** is a sentence with an action verb, the subject performs the action denoted by the verb.
 
 
• ***​******For example***: "The farmer is doing his job".
 
 
 
• ​Passive voice - A*** passive voice ***is a sentence with an action verb, the subject is no longer active but is instead being acted upon by the verb.
 
 
• ​***For example***: "The job is done by a farmer".

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct collocation.

Holm, a Danish traveller, had made a/an ________ replica of the tablet, which in 1908 was deposited in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**exact**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct option is "***exact***".
 
• The ***complete sentence*** would be:
 
 
• Holm, a Danish traveler, had made an ***exact*** replica of the tablet, which in 1908 was deposited in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
 
 
 
• ​Exact refers to ***conformity*** to reality, an accepted standard, or the truth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A*** collocation*** is a grouping of two or more frequently occurring words.
 
• When used frequently by native English speakers, these combinations simply sound "***right***".
 
• Other combinations, however, could sound "***wrong***" and strange.
 
• For instance, we say "***heavy rain***" but not "strong rain" because it doesn't sound right.
 
• Similarly, we say "***do exercise***" but not "make exercise".
 
• ***Adjectives***,*** verbs***,*** nouns***,*** adverbs***, and other word types can all be used to create collocations.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Poor posture may strain neck muscles, whether you're leaning over your computer or hunching over your workstation.

B. However, neck pain may occasionally be an indication of a more serious issue.

C. Neck pain is a frequent problem among many people these days.

D. If your neck pain is accompanied by numbness or lack of strength in your arms or hands, or if you experience shooting pain into your shoulder or down your arm, you should seek medical attention.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"CABD"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a **paragraph** is **coherent**, there are **no jarring shifts or jumps** between **any of the sentences.**
 
• The **correct order** will be as follows:
 
 
• **Neck pain** is a frequent problem among many people these days.
 
• **Poor posture** may strain neck muscles, whether you're leaning over **your computer** or **hunching** over your workstation.
 
• However, **neck pain** may occasionally be an **indication** of a more serious issue.
 
• **If your neck pain** is accompanied by **numbness or lack of strength** in your arms or hands, or if you experience shooting pain into your shoulder or down your arm, you should seek **medical attention.**
 
 
 
• ​Therefore the correct order is **CABD**.
